paragraphs: Decision center: the work of Education Teachers, Postsecondary is to turn these front-end conditions — the subject knowledge of education and educational research methods, the needs of students and teachers and departments, curriculum and teaching and assessment data, research and academic service and teaching workload and academic norms — into executable, reviewable and accountable teaching, research and academic service results: first determine the curriculum and teaching and assessment objectives by subject direction and program goals, then prepare syllabi and assignments and lecture notes and teach and organize discussions and practice, then set, administer and grade examinations and give feedback, and during that period conduct educational research and write and submit and revise and respond to reviewers' comments, then advise students and supervise fieldwork and internships and research and take part in academic conferences and peer review, and finally take part in department curriculum and degree and accreditation work and improve courses based on teaching and research data and complete handover. The focus of judgment is not "can I get through a class", but whether, along the chain of "teaching—research—academic service and student advising", one can hold four things — subject accuracy, teaching responsibility, academic integrity and verifiable evidence — and leave a checkable record at every step.

Worth trying first: being willing to be responsible for others' learning and growth and to accept questioning from students and peers and departments; being able to switch pace among lesson preparation and teaching and grading and research and papers and service; being willing to act according to academic norms and program goals and teaching rules and to handle academic integrity and grades and teaching evaluation matters; and being able to accept the long hours of lesson preparation and papers and conferences driven by semester and proposal defense and submission and review and assessment cycles.

Think carefully: if you expect this job to be just reading the lecture notes through and leaving, or to be only about research with no concern for teaching, or you are unwilling to act according to academic norms and teaching rules and procedures, or you avoid responsibility for academic integrity and student advising, or you treat student teaching evaluations or paper counts as the only conclusion and make major decisions on that basis, or you find it hard to keep patience and professional boundaries under multi-party review and public deliberation, then the actual experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk check: using the fictional course materials and anonymous teaching and evaluation and assignment data provided on this page, complete a paper exercise of "writing a lesson plan for one session of a course design, plus assessment criteria, plus grading of assignments, plus an academic integrity check", verifying only whether you are willing to check items one by one against objectives and data and norms and to honestly mark uncertainty. The exercise uses fictional materials, does not constitute a grade or academic disciplinary or appointment conclusion, and is not equivalent to a teaching qualification or academic authorization.

Decision center: whether the subject direction and curriculum and teaching and assessment data and student needs can be turned into teaching and research and academic service results that students and peers and departments can all take up and review.

The work rhythm is jointly determined by semester and lesson preparation and teaching and grading and proposal defense and submission and review and assessment points; lesson preparation and papers and conferences and grading are numerous, and the investment in teaching and research and service needs to be documented and balanced.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 25-1081.00 Education Teachers, Postsecondary. Adjacent roles — instructional coordinators (25-9031), education administrators, postsecondary (11-9033), training and development managers (11-3131), school psychologists (19-3034), education administrators, kindergarten through secondary (11-9032), educational, guidance and career counselors and advisors (21-1012), special education teachers (25-2050), and primary and secondary school teachers (25-2xxx / 25-3xxx) — have different objects and authorizations; this occupation is not equivalent to an education administrator or an instructional coordinator. Postsecondary appointment and teaching qualifications and academic authorization follow the laws and regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and institutional rules, are not inferred from job titles, and no one may issue legal or financial or personnel disciplinary conclusions externally beyond authorization.

You can use AI as a controlled aid for lesson preparation and literature and data, but you cannot treat generated content as unreviewed course content or grade assessment or research conclusions; student grades and academic integrity and papers and external review remain the responsibility of named teachers and departments and institutions.

The fit judgment should be made by combining whether you can take responsibility for students' learning and research and academic service, whether you can act according to academic norms and teaching rules and data, whether you can communicate under multi-party review and student teaching evaluations and escalate according to the rules, and whether you are clear about the boundaries of your authority over grades and academic integrity and papers and external review; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of "being good at exams" or "loving to read"; all of this must be confirmed in supervised teaching and research and academic service experience.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real decisions about courses and grades and academic integrity and appointment and funding and discipline must be undertaken by personnel who hold the appropriate qualifications and act in accordance with the laws and regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and institutional rules and the requirements of education administrative departments; individuals may not issue legal or financial or personnel disciplinary conclusions externally beyond their authorization, and this page does not constitute any academic or legal or financial or employment advice.

The work object of this occupation is postsecondary students and departments, with high-frequency interaction with the academic community: the subject knowledge of education and educational research methods, the needs of students and teachers and departments, curriculum and teaching and assessment data, research projects and papers and conferences and peer review, teaching workload and academic service and academic norms, and proposal and degree and accreditation and assessment arrangements. The output is teaching and research results that meet program goals and academic norms: teaching and discussions and practice carried out according to the curriculum and program goals, course and teaching improvements and course designs formed from data, examination setting and grading and grade and feedback records completed according to the rules, research and papers and project and conference materials completed according to the norms, and reviewable teaching and research and academic service records. The basis for judgment is subject knowledge and academic norms and program goals and data, not personal preference or job title.

Judgment one: whether the subject direction aligns with the curriculum and program goals — whether course content and teaching and assessment objectives are determined by subject knowledge and program goals and assessment data, rather than taught by habit.

Judgment two: whether teaching and discussion and practice are evidence-based — whether teaching and improvement are organized according to subject knowledge and curriculum and teaching and assessment requirements, rather than by improvising.

Judgment three: whether examination setting and grading and grades and feedback follow the rules — whether grading and feedback are done and documented according to grading criteria and teaching rules and procedures, rather than decided on the spot.

Judgment four: whether research and papers and projects hold to the norms — whether research and writing and submission are carried out according to academic norms and ethics and data requirements, rather than patched together or padded.

Judgment five: whether advising and academic service and academic integrity are upheld — whether students are advised and review and service are undertaken according to program goals and academic norms, rather than avoided or bypassing procedures.

Judgment six: whether the boundaries of data and compliance and external review and discipline are upheld — whether data are used according to laws and regulations and data authority and privacy and student and research record requirements, without issuing academic or legal or financial or personnel disciplinary conclusions externally beyond authorization, and seeking instructions and reporting according to the rules when something is abnormal.

Environment and rhythm: mainly postsecondary classrooms and offices and laboratories and online teaching, with high-frequency communication with students and peers and departments; the rhythm is driven by semester and lesson preparation and teaching and grading and proposal defense and submission and review and assessment points, and lesson preparation and papers and conferences and grading are numerous; specific arrangements and hours follow the institution and jurisdiction.

The work of Education Teachers, Postsecondary can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first category is teaching: determine course content and teaching and assessment objectives by subject direction and program goals and assessment data, prepare syllabi and assignments and lecture notes and practice materials, teach and organize discussions and seminars and practice, set and administer and grade examinations and give feedback, update course content and teaching methods, and improve courses under feedback from students and peers and teaching centers. The second category is research: conduct educational research and literature reviews and data collection and analysis, write and submit and revise papers and monographs and reports, apply for and carry out research projects and funding, take part in academic conferences and peer review and academic exchange, and comply with research ethics and data and authorship norms. The third category is student advising and academic service: advise students on course selection and studies and research methods and papers and proposal defense and oral defense, supervise fieldwork and internships and research and competitions and student societies, take part in department curriculum and degree and accreditation and admissions and program work, undertake review and consultation and academic organization and public service, and keep good records and handover of teaching and research and service. All three work areas proceed within subject and academic norms and program goals and data.

Core purpose

To turn subject knowledge and educational research methods and student needs into executable and reviewable and accountable teaching and research and academic service results: clear curriculum and assessment objectives, evidence-based teaching and feedback, research and papers that hold to the norms, advising and service according to the rules, and reports and discipline that hold the boundaries.

Core purposes of adjacent roles: instructional coordinators support curriculum and instruction and teacher development; postsecondary education administrators keep institutional and academic affairs running; training and development managers improve corporate employee capabilities; school psychologists safeguard students' psychological and learning support; primary and secondary education administrators safeguard school running and teaching; educational, guidance and career counselors help students with academic and career planning; special education teachers provide education and support for students with special needs.
Main objects and basis

The objects are the subject knowledge of education and educational research methods, students and teachers and departments, curriculum and teaching and assessment data, research projects and papers and conferences and peer review, teaching workload and academic service and academic norms; the basis is subject knowledge and academic norms and program goals and data.

Objects and basis of adjacent roles: curriculum and instruction and teacher needs (curriculum and teaching standards and teacher professional standards); higher education institutions and faculty and students and academic affairs (higher education regulations and institutional rules); corporate employees and business objectives (corporate training and human resources rules); student psychology and learning (psychological assessment and ethics norms); primary and secondary schools and teachers and students (compulsory education and teacher regulations and district rules); student academics and careers (academic and employment guidance norms); students with special needs (special education regulations and individualized education programs).

Teaching → research → student advising and academic service (including course improvement and department work).

Teaching and discussions and practice carried out according to the curriculum and program goals, course and teaching improvements formed from data, examination setting and grading and grade and feedback records completed according to the rules, research and papers and project and conference materials completed according to the norms, and reviewable teaching and research and academic service records.

Outputs of adjacent roles: curriculum and instruction coordination and teacher support records; institutional and academic and compliance records; corporate training plans and effectiveness evaluations; student psychological assessment and intervention records; primary and secondary school running and teaching records; student academic and career guidance records; individualized education programs and support records.
Responsible party

This occupation is responsible for organizing teaching and research and advising according to subject and academic norms and data and for student grades and academic integrity and papers and review; departments and academic committees and competent authorities bear management responsibility for curriculum and degrees and appointment and academic discipline and compliance conclusions according to laws and regulations and institutional rules.

Responsibility of adjacent roles: borne by the heads of each institution and the relevant professionals according to their respective laws and regulations and institutional rules, on different bases of authorization.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with students and teachers and departments and supervisors and teaching centers and academic committees and journals and funders and conference organizers, adjusting priorities according to semester and proposal defense and submission and review and assessment points; academic integrity and data and over-authorization matters are escalated and reported according to the rules.

Collaboration of adjacent roles: with teachers and teaching and research groups (instructional coordinators); with departments and faculty and students and academic affairs (postsecondary administration); with human resources and corporate departments (training and development managers); with teachers and parents and medical staff (school psychologists); with teachers and parents and supervisors (primary and secondary schools); with teachers and further study and employment agencies (guidance counselors); with parents and medical and rehabilitation staff (special education teachers).
Conclusion boundaries

Must determine courses and assessment according to subject and program goals and data, must organize teaching and discussion according to subject and teaching requirements, must grade and give feedback according to grading criteria and teaching rules, must conduct research and writing according to academic norms and ethics and data, must advise students and take part in review and service according to program goals and academic norms, must use student and research data according to data authority and privacy, and must not issue academic or legal or financial or personnel disciplinary conclusions externally beyond authorization.
The boundaries of adjacent roles are determined by their own objects and laws and regulations and institutional rules; similar institutions or job titles do not mean interchangeable duties.
In this work, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be checked?

Common errors cluster in four categories: first, the subject direction is disconnected from the curriculum and program goals, leading to inconsistent course content and assessment requirements and unfounded improvement; second, teaching and students are assessed by impression rather than data and observation, leading to distorted teaching and student attrition; third, examination setting and grading and grades and feedback are not handled according to the rules and procedures, leading to grade disputes and risks to fairness and academic integrity; fourth, research and papers and projects do not hold to the norms, or student and research data and external review overstep boundaries, leading to academic integrity and privacy and accountability risks. The way to check is that each item has a reviewable basis: course content and assessment objectives and course improvement plans, teaching and discussion and teaching evaluation records, examination setting and grading and grade and feedback records, research and paper and submission and project records, and academic integrity and student and research data and compliance records — not memory or verbal agreement.

This table compares Education Teachers, Postsecondary with six adjacent roles that are easily confused in institutional names and educational duties, or that have rotation and transfer relationships, row by row across core work and outputs, key differences, and basis for choice. The purpose of the comparison is not to rank them, but to explain their respective service objects and authorization and compliance boundaries — in particular, legal adjudication power and financial decision power and personnel disciplinary power and academic disciplinary power cannot be borne by this occupation as well.

When comparing, three things govern: first, the work object (curriculum and instruction and teacher needs, higher education institutions and faculty and students and academic affairs, corporate employees and training needs, student psychology and learning, primary and secondary schools and teachers and students, student academics and careers, students with special needs); second, the basis and authorization (subject knowledge and academic norms and program goals and data, curriculum and teaching standards and teacher professional standards, higher education regulations and institutional rules, corporate training and human resources rules, psychological assessment and ethics norms, compulsory education and teacher regulations and district rules, academic and employment guidance norms, and special education regulations and individualized education programs, each as applicable); third, outputs and responsibility (who is responsible for teaching and research in higher education, who for curriculum and instruction coordination, who for institutional and academic affairs, who for corporate training, who for student psychology, who for primary and secondary school running, who for student academic and career guidance, and who for the education and support of students with special needs). Where the three conflict, the actual duties of the post and the laws and regulations and institutional rules govern.

The basis for choice can follow three threads: if you want to undertake the teaching and research of education and teacher education related courses in a higher education institution, this page's occupation is the closest; if you want to work in curriculum and instruction coordination, institutional and academic affairs, corporate training, student psychology, primary and secondary school running, academic and career guidance, or the education of students with special needs, then instructional coordinators, education administrators postsecondary, training and development managers, school psychologists, education administrators kindergarten through secondary, educational guidance and career counselors and advisors, and special education teachers are adjacent paths. When transferring posts, what must be filled in is the object and laws and regulations and authorization, not only subject knowledge.

Observation signal two: willing to act according to the rules for student and research data and grades and academic integrity and academic norms, and confirming before acting where grades and academic misconduct and papers and review are involved.

Observation signal three: able to stay careful about subject and data and procedures under multi-party review and public deliberation and semester and submission cycles, and not skip checks because of schedule pressure.

Observation signal four: able to accept the long hours of lesson preparation and papers and conferences driven by semester and lesson preparation and teaching and grading and proposal defense and submission and review and assessment cycles, and willing to do records and reports and handover.

Trainable capabilities include curriculum and teaching and assessment design, teaching and discussion and seminars and experiments and practice, examination setting and grading and feedback, literature and data and research methods, papers and projects and academic writing, student advising and academic service and academic norms, and student and research data and privacy and records.

Within 40 minutes, write a lesson plan for a course design and assessment criteria and assignment grading and an academic integrity check, and fill out one form for examination setting and grading and grades and data and abnormality reporting.

items.title: Entry case material: one fictional course design check

values: Day 1: understand the materials
Read the fictional course materials and anonymous grade and teaching evaluation data and institutional materials, circle uncertain items and write out a question list.
Day 2: objectives and curriculum
Lay out course content and assessment objectives and teaching steps by subject and program goals, and mark items to be confirmed.
Day 3: teaching and grading
Write a section of course teaching and examination setting and grading and feedback notes based on subject and assignment data.
Day 4: research and writing
Write a literature review or research design and data and authorship key points according to academic norms.
Day 5: grades and compliance
Fill out one form for examination setting and grading and grades and academic integrity and data and authorship and abnormality reporting.
Day 6: timed repeat
Redo it under time limits and record energy and error types.
Day 7: compare and decide
Compare the two versions and write down continue / be cautious / stop and the reasons.

entries: Day 1 judgment: whether the uncertain items in the materials were honestly marked, rather than filled in by guessing.

description.text: Education Teachers, Postsecondary (O*NET-SOC 25-1081.00) undertake the teaching and research of education and teacher education related courses in higher education institutions: determining course content and assessment objectives by subject direction and program goals and assessment data, preparing syllabi and assignments and lecture notes and teaching and organizing discussions and practice, setting and administering and grading examinations and giving feedback, conducting educational research and literature and data work and writing and submitting and revising papers and monographs, applying for and carrying out research projects, advising students on course selection and studies and papers and proposal defense and oral defense, and taking part in curriculum and degree and accreditation and admissions work. United States basis: BLS 2025 wage data median 75,350 USD per year (median only); 2024 employment about 74,900, 2024—2034 projection "slower than average (1% to 2%)" with about 5,600 projected openings; preparation level Job Zone Five, interest code SI. Mainland China: higher education post appointment and teaching qualifications and assessment and training are carried out in accordance with the Higher Education Law and the Regulations on Personnel Management of Public Institutions and the provisions of education administrative departments and institutions; public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage basis, and this page visibly marks the gap in the relevant places.

subject.name: Education Teachers, Postsecondary
subject.summary: Education Teachers, Postsecondary (United States side O*NET-SOC 25-1081.00, Education Teachers, Postsecondary) is a teaching and research post in higher education institutions: teaching and research of education and teacher education related courses in higher education institutions; the work includes determining course content and teaching and assessment objectives by subject direction and program goals and assessment data, preparing syllabi and assignments and lecture notes and practice materials, teaching and organizing discussions and seminars and practice, setting and administering and grading examinations and giving feedback, updating course content and teaching methods, conducting educational research and literature reviews and data collection and analysis, writing and submitting and revising papers and monographs and reports, applying for and carrying out research projects and funding, taking part in academic conferences and peer review and academic exchange, advising students on course selection and studies and research methods and papers and proposal defense and oral defense, supervising fieldwork and internships and research and competitions and student societies, taking part in department curriculum and degree and accreditation and admissions and program work, undertaking review and consultation and academic organization and public service, and keeping good records and handover of teaching and research and service. United States basis: BLS 2025 wage data median 75,350 USD per year (that source provides only the median and does not provide the 10/25/75/90 percentiles or an hourly basis); the O*NET summary page gives 2024 employment of about 74,900, a 2024—2034 projection of "slower than average (Slower than average, 1% to 2%)" and about 5,600 projected openings for 2024—2034 (total for the projection period); the preparation level is Job Zone Five (SVP 8.0 and above), education feedback is 90% doctoral degrees and 9% master's degrees and 1% bachelor's degrees, the interest code is SI, and there are 25 tasks. Mainland China basis: higher education post appointment and qualification and assessment and training are carried out in accordance with the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Personnel Management of Public Institutions and the relevant provisions of education administrative departments and institutions, and teaching in a teaching post should obtain a higher education institution teaching qualification in accordance with the Teachers Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage basis corresponding to this occupation, and this page preserves the gap faithfully, with the industry average wage serving only as a visible industry proxy.
